title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
notes: Almost nothing here is testable, which is the point of including it. Every claim is about how to pretrain a large language model, and the effects are created by data and compute scale. A good triage should reject nearly all of this; an agent that shrinks BERT pretraining to a CPU budget would be measuring noise.

claims.text: Training BERT longer, with bigger batches and more data, improves downstream task performance.
claims.notes: Explicitly a claim about scale. Shrinking removes the very thing being claimed.

claims.text: Removing the next sentence prediction objective matches or improves downstream performance compared to keeping it.
claims.notes: A clean ablation in shape, but each arm requires pretraining a transformer on a large corpus. Not feasible on a small CPU budget.

claims.text: Dynamic masking performs comparably to or slightly better than the static masking used in the original BERT.
claims.notes: The reported difference is a few tenths of a point after full pretraining; unreachable at reduced scale.

claims.text: Training on full sentences without the next-sentence-prediction loss outperforms the original segment-pair input format.
claims.notes: Again requires pretraining runs per arm.

claims.text: RoBERTa reaches 88.5 on the GLUE leaderboard.
A larger byte-level BPE vocabulary performs slightly worse on some tasks but is preferred for its universality.
claims.notes: Mixes an empirical comparison with a design preference, and still requires pretraining.
